lede: The biggest thing on the government calendar this week is Mountain Village Town Council taking up first reading of an ordinance that would move Housing Authority fees out of municipal code and into an annually updated fee schedule — a structural shift in how affordable housing costs get set. Close behind: the San Miguel County Housing Code Update SSR holds its eighth working session on stripping Land Use Code barriers to workforce housing, HARC takes up a potential demolition and new construction application for Rebekah Hall — the historic Town-owned building where HARC itself meets — and the BOCC weighs in on a view-plain MOU tied to a 1999 settlement.

notable.stake: Policy vote on how subpar mitigation bedrooms get handled under Housing Guidelines.
Working session shaping county code changes that govern workforce housing production.
HARC reviews potential demolition of historic Town-owned Rebekah Hall building.
BOCC considers view-plain MOU and immigration/redistricting constitutional amendment discussion.
Two public hearings: Curry PUD and a parcel subdivision application in Ouray County.
First reading of ordinance shifting MVHA fees out of municipal code — changes how housing costs are set.
